newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA INFLATION ACCELERATES TO 3.7 PCT IN JULY.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA INFLATION ACCELERATES TO 3.7 PCT IN JULY.

text.p: Bulgaria's monthly consumer price inflation accelerated to 3.7 percent in July from 0.8 percent in June, the National Statistics Institute (NSI) said on Monday.
Cumulative inflation for the first seven months was 505.6 percent. A year on year inflation figure for July will be available later this month.
BULGARIAN CONSUMER PRICES JULY JUNE JULY'96

BREAKDOWN

Fresh fruit prices posted the biggest month on month rise
among foods with 53.8 percent.
Cooking oil rose by 30.7 percent after a 37.7 percent rise
in June and milk and cheese rose 13-14 percent.
Prices of potatoes fell 18.8 percent and tomatoes fell 8.4
percent.
Consumer price inflation for 1997 was assumed at 566
percent in this year's budget. Annual inflation for 1996 was
310.8 percent.
The projection was made under a currency board system, a
form of a fixed exchange rate mechanism prescribed by the
International Monetary Fund (IMF) to restore confidence in the
lev, to curb inflation and to stabilise the economy.
Under the system introduced on July 1 the lev was pegged at
1,000 per mark as anchor and central bank lending to the
government and commercial banks was banned to prevent the
printing of money.
Under a memorandum of economic policies agreed with the IMF
monthly inflation was expected near two percent at the end of
this year.
